tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs
tweets.text: We shipped four updates to Claude Managed Agents this week. First, you can now set a budget for sessions to keep spend predictable. Sessions that hit the limit pause with a budget_reached event, you can raise the budget to resume. Video

tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs
tweets.text: Managed Agents now load skills from your attached repositories. If you already keep skills in .claude/skills/ for Claude Code, Managed Agent sessions pick them up automatically at start.

tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs
tweets.text: Lastly, you can now give a Claude Managed Agent an advisor: a stronger model it can call mid-session for a second opinion. Add one line to the roster and the working agent gets an advisor.

tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs
tweets.text: New in Claude Code: your sessions can now message each other. Instead of having to re-explain yourself in another session, you can now tell Claude to do it. It sends a summary (not your history or files), and the other session picks it up mid-task. Video

tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs
tweets.text: It goes both ways: you can also ask another session a question and get the answer back in your active session. Claude can also message another session on its own, e.g. when a change it just made affects what that session is working on.

tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs

tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs
tweets.text: Starting August 14, auto mode will be the default permission mode in Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Team users. Auto mode reviews shell commands and actions with a separate classifier. In testing, it caught 89% of dangerous commands. Manual approval caught 14%.

tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs
tweets.text: You’ll get an in-app notification when the default flips. If you’ve already set a default permission mode, Claude will ask before changing anything. You can still switch modes with Shift+Tab anytime. Admins can pin defaultMode (or disable auto mode entirely) in managed settings

tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs
tweets.text: Auto mode also pairs well with models that excel at long-running tasks, like Opus 5. The model can plan and execute multi-hour tasks, but that only pays off if the session doesn't stop at every tool call waiting for you. With auto mode, you can kick off a task (or multiple in parallel) and come back to completed PRs ready for your review.

tweets.creator: @ClaudeDevs
tweets.text: Auto mode runs a classifier on every tool call, which uses a small number of extra tokens. As of today, that classifier overhead no longer counts toward your usage limits on Pro, Max, and Team plans. This change will come to Enterprise plans and API users once auto mode is the default for those users, too.
